newsitem.title: FRANCE: Minister says France Telecom stake sale must go on.
newsitem.headline: Minister says France Telecom stake sale must go on.

text.p: French Telecommunications Minister Francois Fillon said plans by opposition Socialists to stop the sale of a stake in France Telecom if they won the upcoming parliamentary election were unrealistic.

"The Socialists' approach is unrealistic, dangerous for the company and apparently inspired by their electoral accord with the Communist party," Fillon said in an interview with financial daily Les Echos to be published on Wednesday.
The Socialists have pledged to halt the privatisation of France Telecom and other state-owned companies if they win the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election called by French President Jacques Chirac.
Most opinion polls show the Socialists losing the election.
Fillon said the privatisation of other national telephone operators across Europe made it impossible for France to abandon its plan to float 30 to 35 percent of France Telecom after the election.

"It is unimaginable that France Telecom be the only operator remaining completely in the hands of the state. It would be an unbearable constraint and (would impose) quickly the risk of calling into question international accords, notably with Deutsche Telekom and Sprint," Fillon said.
He also said the timing of the sale could not be changed.

"There is no give in the calendar. The opening of the capital must absolutely take place before summer, first because we must not destabilise the company in its preparations for competition, next because there are other privatisations to come in Europe."
The European telecommunications market will open for full competition in 1998.
Fillon added that the government still planned to sell a second tranche of France Telecom at a later date.
